model_interpretation.claim: The serial coarse-root loop may leave cores idle when recursive shading workloads differ by tile. This candidate tests dynamic one-tile work assignment across root tiles, with run()'s thread count as the cap; the serial path is retained for one thread. It does not parallelize depth-bound rows, so its effect can be evaluated independently of that approach.

items.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare parallel work decomposition while preserving the requested thread budget: worksharing the independent coarse-root tiles (including static versus dynamic scheduling) and parallelizing the independent base-level depth-bound rows in MinMaxZTree::Update. Measure each approach independently and, if useful, measure a combination rather than assuming additive gains; higher tree levels still depend on completed lower levels. Keep culling and shading algorithms unchanged, pass run()'s thread count as an upper bound, avoid unnecessary overhead at one thread, and preserve disjoint writes. Validate full output and correctness at 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
